title: Fatal engine startup crash is reported to the user as a timeout (exposed by a SIGILL on pre-AVX2 CPUs)
description: ensureServerRunning (js/services/comfyController.js:393) polls for readiness and throws a generic timeout. It does not distinguish a child process that has ALREADY EXITED from one still starting, so two unrelated fatal crashes reached the user identically as "ComfyUI server failed to become ready in time": a missing sqlalchemy (MPI-414 aftermath) and a SIGILL. Both died in under a second with the real traceback sitting in app.log. FIX: capture the engine child exit code/signal and its last error lines and surface those, failing fast when the process is dead. Exposed by ComfyUI core failing to start on a pre-AVX2 x86_64 CPU - kornia_rs 0.1.14 SIGILLs at import via nodes.py init_builtin_extra_nodes -> comfy_extras/nodes_post_processing.py -> kornia -> kornia_rs (core, not a custom node). Measured on an i3-2367M with avx but no avx2/fma; kornia_rs 0.1.9 imports clean. A GLOBAL kornia_rs pin is REJECTED - it penalises every user on every platform and fights the MPI-413/MPI-217 drift class. The exact ISA floor is UNCONFIRMED (no objdump on the box); do not publish a hardware requirement until the wheel is disassembled. Not Linux-specific: the same package is pulled through ComfyUI core on Windows x86_64. Related: MPI-414, MPI-413, MPI-198.

attention.reason: Fixed and live-verified 2026-07-31: real crash caught in 3s with the cause captured, vs a 60s timeout before. CPU-specific halves dropped per user call.
